lawyer:
Md. Abdus Salam Khan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants 
Sayyid Shahid Hossain, Advocate, instructed by A. S. M. Khalequzzaman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Abdul Quddus and another ----- Appellants
Vs.
Latif Bawany Jute Mills Ltd. & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
M. M. Ruhul Amin, J.:- This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and decree dated 18.11.2001 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 434 of 1999 allowing the appeal in part and thereby decreeing the plaintiffs suit for TK. 3,98,132.44/- and dismissing the cross objection filed by the plaintiffs. 

 5. The trial court decreed the suit for TK. 21,48,488/- for handing and carrying of jute, including truck fare for 52 days, finding inter alia, that the appellants could prove their case for the said amount and for the rest amount, the appellants could not prove their case. The appellants then took First Appeal No. 434 of 1999 before the High Court Division. After considering and assessing the oral and documentary evidence the High Court Division found that the appellants were entitled to get Tk. 3,73,132.44 for the price of 63566 kgs of wheat which were filed by the mill authority and Tk. 25,000/- as earnest money which was deposited by the appellants for the purpose of works orders dated 02.07.1987 for the year 1986-1987. Accordingly, the High Court Division allowed the appeal in part and decreed the suit by modifying the judgment and decree of the trial Court and the High Court Division decreed Tk. 3,98,132.44/- only and dismissed the cross objection filed by the appellants herein. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the High Court Division did not pass a decree for 11,91,704.00/-which was admittedly deposited by the appellants in the Bangladesh Bank, vide chalan dated 20.09.1998 for the year 1987-88 for the purpose of lifting of wheat-being 2,03016 Kgs, and further submission that P.W. 2 Abdur Rouf Miah, an employee of the District Controller of Food deposed that he produced chalan No. 6-1-1/8 dated 20.09.1988 for 203 ton and 16 kgs of wheat worth TK. 11,91,704.00/- but those goods were delivered to the management of the mills and the further submissions that the defendant No. 5, Yousuf Mia received the wheat on behalf of the Mill Authority on 21.09.1982 to 25.09.1988 by putting his own signature in the delivery orders but those have not been considered by the trial court and the High Court Division and the further submissions that the mill authority had no paper to show that the plaintiffs took delivery of 1,39,550 Kgs of wheat on 21.08.1988 and 22.08.1988 and it is rather admitted by them that the defendant No. 5 took delivery of the said wheat for the mill authority. 

 8. The plaintiffs claimed a sum of TK. 1,00,000,00.00/- as damages for defamation and malicious prosecution. It is undisputed that the criminal case, being Tejgoan P.S. Case No. 49S(9)88 initiated in connection with the lifting of the wheat by the trucks of the plaintiffs is still pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka as proceeding of that case was stayed by the High Court Division at the instance of the plaintiff No. 1 vide Ext.6 and as such the criminal case has not yet ended in acquittal. The plaintiff is, therefore, not entitled to a decree one account of damages and compensation for malicious prosecution and for defaming their reputation. The High Court Division held that if the criminal case had ended in acquittal, even then the plaintiffs had to establish that there was no sufficient reason or cause to initiate the criminal case by the defendants against the plaintiffs. In the circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division correctly assessed the materials on record in connection with the claim of the plaintiffs on account of damage and compensation or malicious prosecution or defamation and rightly dismissed the claim and we have nothing to interfere with in this regard. 

 11. The plaintiffs claimed an amount of TK. 14,95,642/- as price of wheat on the ground that they did not take delivery of wheat in question on 21.09.1988 and 22.09.1988 from the Government godown to be carried to the mill premises for distribution among the workers of the mill. It is undisputed that there is a contract/agreement between the mill authority and the plaintiff No. 1 for carrying and distribution of ration articles to the workers of the mill vide Ext. 2 dated 15.08.1988. We have perused Clauses III, IV, VI, VII and IX of Ext.2 which clearly show that the plaintiff shall carry the goods from the Government godown to the mill premises at their own expenses and shall keep proper account of all goods and articles drawn by him from the Government godown and shall maintain proper and correct accounts of the sales of the goods as prescribed by the Government and shall furnish statement/ return as required by them and if any irregularities or malpractice are committed by the plaintiff or his men in dealing with their ration articles and food stuffs the contractor shall be solely and exclusively responsible for such and necessary action shall be taken against him and in the evident of violation, in addition to other remedies at their option cancel the contract/agreement including forfeiture of the security money. It is also provided in Ext. 2 that while carrying ration, commodities and food stuffs from the Government godown to ration shop inside the mill the contractor (plaintiff) should get the truck entry recorded in the gate by the security and the number of the bags etc. should also be recorded in the ration shop by the dealing personnel of the mill. It appears from the records, that the plaintiffs did not furnish any account of sale of the goods and food stuffs which were lifted on 21.09.1988 and 22.09.1988. They also could not produce any evidence to the effect that the wheat lifted from the government godown and loaded in his truck and hired trucks on 21.09.1988 and 22.09.1988 were carried to the mill premises and distributed to the employees and workers of the mills and also could not prove that they got their trucks entry recorder in the gate of the Mill. The plaintiff also could not prove that there is any practice for obtaining any receipt from him by the representative of them ill in whose presence the ration articles were loaded in his trucks at the government godown gate. The High Court Division considered the evidence of P.W. 5 Abdur Rour Mia, an employee of the office of District Controller of Food, Dhaka and not an employee of the Central Storage Depot (C.S.D) Tejgaon. He produced photo copies of some papers without producing the originals of the same which in our view the High Court Division rightly left out of consideration. The High Court Division also considered the evidence of D.W. 7 Afttab Uddin who produced godown delivery register Ext. A(1). The Authenticity of his document had not been questioned by the plaintiffs and no suggestion was given to the D.W. 7 that this registers is not the register signed by D.W 12, Yusuf and D.W. 12 was also not confronted with this document Ext. A(1). Thus the contention of the plaintiffs that on 11.09.1988 and 22.09.1988 the defendants in collusion with each other lifted the wheat from Government godown and misappropriated the same has not been proved at all. The High Court Division on correct assessment of the evidence came to the finding that the plaintiff are not entitled to any decree on account of the money deposited for wheat lifted on 21.09.1988 and 22.09.1988 and the plaintiffs are also not entitled to revive any commission for their failure to fulfill the terms of the contract. The two trucks belonging to the plaintiffs were seized by the police in connection with the criminal case and as such the trucks were detained and the plaintiffs got the trucks released from the police custody by order of the court in which the criminal case is still pending and in our opinion the High Court Division rightly held that the plaintiffs were not entitled to claim any amount on this count. 

 12. Regarding the claim of the plaintiff for the quantum of wheat namely 63,566 Kgs lifted on 24.09.1988 and 25.09.1988 by mill authority and loaded in the plaintiffs trucks which the plaintiffs earlier placed at the gate of the godown, the defendants contention is that at the presence of the officers of the mill at the gate of the godown the plaintiffs left the godown premises and hence they had to load the wheat in the trucks of the plaintiffs already placed at the gate of the godown and this quantum of wheat was seized by police in connection with the criminal case and the wheat was sold in auction by order of he high Court Division, Ext. 6 and the sale proceeds of the wheat are lying with the court. The High Court Division held that the plaintiffs are entitled to et a decree for TK. 3,73,132.44 being price of the quantum of wheat lifted on 24.09.1988 and 25.09.1988 by the mill management and an amount of TK. 25,000/- deposited as earnest money deposited in connection with the transaction to be made under Ext. 2 as the amount was not forfeited according to the terms of ext. 2. 

 13. In our view, upon correct assessment of the evidence on record the High Court Division took a correct view in the matter as the plaintiffs did not lift the wheat on 24.09.1988 and 25.09.1988, rather the same was lifted by the mill management and accordingly held that the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree for Tk. 3,73,132.44/- as the price of 63,566 kgs of wheat taken delivery by the defendants and an amount of Tk. 25. 25,000/- as earnest money deposited in connection with the transaction to be made under Ext. 2 as the amount was not forfeited according to the terms of Ext.2.
